name: GCSE History (Pearson Edexcel 1HI0)

selected_options.paper_1_thematic_and_historic_environmen: Option 10: Crime and Punishment in Britain, c1000-present, with the Whitechapel, c1870-c1900 historic environment
selected_options.note: All four option units are this course's selected options.

material_vintage: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9-1) History 1HI0, specification Issue 6 (June 2024), first teaching September 2016, first certification 2018. Itemised on 2026-09-19 from the published specification PDF: the content of Option 10 (thematic study and Whitechapel historic environment), Option P3 (American West), Option B4 (Early Elizabethan England) and Option 31 (Weimar and Nazi Germany) is itemised bullet by bullet using the spec's own key topics, strands and bullet points, and the assessment overview, assessment objectives, weightings, question-type descriptions and SPaG allocation were read from the same document. Verified against the spec: option content, paper structure, AO wording and weightings, total of 168 marks including 8 SPaG marks. Written from memory of the published papers and specimen materials and flagged for re-verification: the exact mark tariffs per sub-question (4/8/12/16 marks) and the stem wording of each question type, since the spec gives the assessment focus but not every tariff. Factual teaching content (dates, people, events, causes, consequences) is written from secondary knowledge and standard textbook accounts, not from the spec, which lists topics only. Historians' names and interpretations in the Weimar and Nazi Germany interpretations stage summarise well-known published arguments in paraphrase and should be checked against the school's set materials. The spec names no historians, so none are prescribed. Stage test scenarios are original questions in the style of the board, not real past-paper items.
level_source: RQF Level 2 (GCSE, full grade range 1-9 / Foundation+Higher tiers covered), per Ofqual's Register of Regulated Qualifications listing for this specification
framework: Edexcel's own AO1 (knowledge/understanding, 35%), AO2 (explanation/analysis using second-order concepts such as cause, consequence, change, continuity, similarity, difference, significance, 35%), AO3 (source analysis and evaluation, 15%), and AO4 (analysis and evaluation of historical interpretations, 15%, tested only in Paper 3). Three papers: Paper 1 thematic study and historic environment (1h20, 52 marks), Paper 2 period study and British depth study (1h50, 64 marks), Paper 3 modern depth study (1h30, 52 marks); 168 marks in total of which 8 are for spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terminology (4 in Paper 1 Q5/6, 4 in Paper 3 Q3(d)). Extended-writing questions are marked by levels of response.
